title: Reverse Linked List
description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return its new head.
hints: Walk the list and repeatedly flip the current node's next pointer to point at the previous node.
Keep three references: prev, current, next.
solution_approach: Initialize prev = None, curr = head. While curr is not None, save curr.next, set curr.next = prev, advance prev = curr, curr = saved next. After the loop prev is the new head.
common_mistakes: Losing the reference to the next node before rewiring curr.next.
Returning the old head instead of the new head.

brute_force.description: Read all values into a list, reverse the list, then rebuild a new linked list.

better.description: Iterative pointer reversal: keep prev/curr/next references and flip each next pointer in a single pass.

optimal.description: The iterative reversal is optimal (O(N) time, O(1) space). A recursive alternative is cleaner but uses O(N) stack space.
